newsitem.title: USA: NYS offical asks tobacco cos to curb teenage use.
newsitem.headline: NYS offical asks tobacco cos to curb teenage use.

text.p: The New York State comptroller, the sole trustee of the state's $80 billion pension fund, said Wednesday he would conduct a "vigorous campaign" to push shareholder resolutions that aim to curb teenager smoking.

H. Carl McCall, in prepared remarks, said his resolutions will appear before the shareholders of Loews Corp and RJR Nabisco Holdings. But he added that Philip Morris and UST Inc got the Securities and Exchange Commission to issue a "no action" letter, denying their shareholders the right to vote on his resolution.

McCall said he wrote the two companies who got the SEC to allow them not to include his resolution, saying he did not believe it addresssed their litigation strategy, a concern he said they had raised and that shareholders should be able to air their views.

"We do, however, believe it is only appropriate that the company allow its shareholders to be heard on this matter since the issue of teen access to tobacco products is critical to realizing the full value of our substantial investment," McCall said, in a letter to the Philip Morris and UST.
The New York State Common Retirement Fund owns 484,000 shares of Loews stock, 633,000 shares of RJR Nabisco, 4.4 million shares of Philip Morris, and 767,000 shares of UST.
